title: Porta do Sono · Sleeping badly is not normal
metaDesc: Snoring, waking up tired, trouble falling asleep? Four taps, nothing to type — and you know whether to see a doctor, which one in Madeira, and what to tell them. In 5 languages. Free, nothing is stored.
heroTitle: Sleeping badly? Let's see which door to knock on.
heroSub: Four taps, nothing to type. A clear traffic light, the right doctor in Madeira, and a ready phrase to show them — in their language.
introLabel: The first door of the Portas family
introNote: Nothing is stored: your answers stay on your phone.

about.door: Door: four questions by buttons — snoring, daytime sleepiness, blood pressure and weight, age — and a traffic light: fine · worth a visit · don't put it off.
about.show: Show the doctor: a screen in Portuguese with your answers and a ready phrase. Just show your phone — no language barrier.
about.routes: Route: through the SNS (family doctor → specialist) or private care in Madeira — only verified places, with the verification date.
about.private: Private: nothing leaves your phone. No sign-up, no account, no data stored.

disclaimer: This is not medical advice — talk to your doctor.
emergencyLine: Shortness of breath, chest pain or fainting right now — call 112.
honest: No diagnoses, no percentages, no promises. Only whether it's worth going, to whom, and what to say.
shareText: Sleeping badly is not normal. Four taps, nothing to type — and you know which doctor to see in Madeira:
emergency: If you have symptoms right now — call 112
emergencyText: Shortness of breath, chest pain, fainting — this is not for a web page. Call now.

sleep.text: What's going on with your sleep?

o.snore: I snore / I'm told I stop breathing
o.tired: I wake up tired, sleepy during the day
o.insomnia: Hard to fall asleep / I wake at night
o.alarm: 🚨 Shortness of breath, chest pain or fainting — right now

o.drive: I doze off driving / in meetings

o.bp: High blood pressure or on pills

green.sub: Nothing points to a doctor yet. If something changes, come back to this door.

yellow.sub: There is reason to talk to your family doctor — no rush, but don't put it off for months.

red.sub: Worth booking an appointment this week.

why.day.drive: Dozing off while driving or in meetings is the strongest sign that sleep isn't restoring you.
why.sleep.snore: Snoring with pauses in breathing is the first thing a sleep doctor wants to hear about.
why.day.often: Frequent daytime sleepiness usually has a cause at night.
why.sleep.tired: Waking up tired after a full night is reason to ask why.
why.body.bp: High blood pressure and poor sleep often go together.
why.body.weight: Extra weight and a wide neck make snoring more likely.
why.sleep.short: Under 6 hours on a regular basis shows the next day.
why.sleep.insomnia: Trouble falling asleep or waking at night can be solved — it starts with your family doctor.
why.sleep.check: Checking before there are complaints is the best time.

steps.mgf: Book your family doctor — at the health centre or in AppSESARAM.
steps.ref: Show them this screen. If they agree, they refer you to the specialist.
steps.exam: If it's apnoea, they usually order a sleep study — often at home, with a device.

private.price: Price and insurance cover: ask when booking.

doc.title: For the doctor
doc.hint: Show this screen to the doctor — it's in Portuguese. Below, the translation for you.

lead.apneia: I'm here with suspected sleep apnoea.
lead.neutral: I'm here because of my sleep.

a.sleep.snore: I snore or I'm told I stop breathing in my sleep.
a.sleep.tired: I wake up tired and feel sleepy during the day.
a.sleep.insomnia: I have trouble falling asleep and wake up during the night.
a.sleep.short: I sleep less than 6 hours a night.
a.sleep.check: No strong complaints, I want to check my sleep.
a.day.drive: I doze off while driving or in meetings.
a.day.often: I often feel sleepy during the day.
a.day.ok: During the day I feel normal.
a.body.bp: I have high blood pressure or take blood-pressure medication.
a.body.neither: No high blood pressure, not overweight.
a.body.unknown: I don't know my blood pressure.

ask.pneumo: I ask for an assessment and, if you see fit, a referral to a sleep / pulmonology consultation.
ask.mgf: I ask for an assessment and advice on the next step.

doc.note: I speak little Portuguese — please speak slowly or write. Thank you.

mgf.d: Porta do Sono: book and bring the «For the doctor» screen.

repeat.d: 3 months have passed — do the four taps again.

warn.drive: While you're this sleepy, don't get behind the wheel.

flyer.title: Porta do Sono — who it's for and how it works
flyer.h1: Sleeping badly? There's a door for that.
flyer.lead: Porta do Sono is a free page in five languages: four taps and you know whether to see a doctor about your sleep, which one in Madeira — and what to tell them.
who: For people living in Madeira who don't speak Portuguese: the page speaks to the doctor for you.
For those who snore and «it's fine» — and for those sleeping next to them who no longer believe it.
For anyone waking up tired for months who never asked why.
how: Four questions by buttons — nothing to type.
A traffic light: fine · worth a visit · don't put it off — and one sentence why.
«Show the doctor»: a screen in Portuguese with your answers. Just show your phone.
«Where to go»: through the SNS or privately in Madeira — only verified places, with a date.
flyer.wow: With every answer a window lights up in the house. On the fourth, the door opens — and dawn breaks.
flyer.privacy: Nothing is stored. No sign-up, no account. Your answers stay on your phone.
flyer.honest: Not medical advice and not a validated test — guidance to take the first step.
